# Kiṁchandajātaka (Ja 511)

**ID:** Ja 511
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul15.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kiṁchandajātaka* (Ja 511), rendered in English as *What Is Your Desire?*, is a canonical birth story belonging to the Jātaka section of the Pali canon. According to the narrative framework recorded in the commentary, the Buddha related this story while dwelling at Jetavana concerning the observance of fast-days (*uposathakamma*), after numerous male and female lay disciples (*upāsaka* and *upāsikā*) observing the uposatha had gathered in the Dhamma hall to hear the teaching [Fausböll 1891]. The verses begin with the opening phrase *Kiṁchando kimadhippāyo ti* [Fausböll 1891]. At the close of the story's identification of characters (*samodhāna*), the deity (*devatā*) is identified as Uppalavaṇṇā and the ascetic (*tāpaso*) as the Buddha himself in a former existence [Fausböll 1891]. The text is also cited in modern scholarship by K. R. Norman [Norman 1983].

 Automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus identifies 12 matching passages (totalling 3,668 characters) between the canonical text and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (fourth volume, with the longest match spanning §1.4–10.6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus further identifies machine alignments with several Tibetan Buddhist works, including the Tibetan *Jātakamālā* (D4150), Kṣemendra's *Bodhisatvāvadānakalpalatā* (D4155 and D4155-1), and the *Ārya-kuśalamūlaparidhāra-sūtra* (D0101), though these represent automated alignments rather than established historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
